High-level answers below; see attached files and the Drive link for more granular operator-level mappings.

Summary answers (short):
- Subprocessors: attached CSV includes operator name, region, role (control plane, inference, logging). Notable new operator: NimbusOps (in EU) is listed as a potential inference provider for edge routing.
- SOC2: we run SOC2 Type II for both our control plane and hosted inference (link in attachments).
- Data residency / fallback: for hosted customers we route by region; if a region is degraded we failover to the next healthy region per routing policy (we provide 30 days notice for planned operator migrations, see change-notice below).
- KMS: customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated via KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted (Redwood API) uses Redwood-managed keys by default; we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key in private deployments with an enterprise addendum.
- Change-notice: standard policy is 30 days for non-emergency subprocessor changes; emergency or regulatory-driven changes may have shorter notice but we publish follow-up evidence and a fallback plan.

Vanessa / Marcus —

Quick security review and clarifications for Elena's list:

- Encryption: all traffic between customer clients and the Redwood API is TLS 1.3 in transit. Data at rest in hosted inference (token caches, logs) is AES-256. For Private/Dedicated we support FIPS 140-2 HSM integrations.
- KMS/CMK: as noted, CMKs are supported only for Dedicated and Private (customer-managed KMS). Hosted customers can request a key-separation model (enterprise tier) but the default is Redwood-managed keys. We can provide design docs for Bring-Your-Own-Key on dedicated capacity.
- Subprocessor change-notice: our contractual SLA includes 30 calendar days for planned changes. For emergency/regulatory events we commit to immediate notification and a documented mitigation/fallback plan within 48 hours.
- Region failover: policy is to route to the next healthy region; we publish the list of regional operators in the CSV. For customers with strict residency requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with region pinning.
- Evidence links: SOC2 report is for our platform control environment; for per-operator evidence (e.g., NimbusOps) we provide operator-level attestations or equivalency statements where available — if EdgeLine needs operator-specific certificates we will ask NimbusOps to produce them (this is slower).

Risk/ask: if EdgeLine requires CMK for hosted traffic we need to evaluate whether they can accept Dedicated or Private. Also confirm whether the partner (FinPartner) will accept the 30-day change-notice window and emergency escalation flow.

I'll mark the items we can answer now in the worksheet and leave operator-specific evidence as pending.

-karthik
